markers.reading: The party resumes aboard Vindristjarna above Uzgukhar just after dawn on May 12.

evidence.quote: DM: Okay, so we will begin on Vindristjarna. Just past dawn, the ship hovering over— let's see— the orcish city of Uzgukhar. In the desert you can still see below you the the ruined walls, the, um, the pieces of the city, the buildings that were destroyed and and crushed when the massive trebuchet was firing boulders, until {{bolder hero!}} {{Or stop that}} most epic rolls in this entire campaign.
Seeker: True. That was crazy.

DM: But it's, it's— it's early morning. The sun has just risen. There's a lot of activity down below in this not yet super hot part of the day. The city seems vibrant and alive, you can see, you know, orcs running around, repairing the walls. Looking, you know, people looking up and waving at you. They recognize the ship. Nobody seems too surprised to see you, so you guess that Faldrak or somebody warned orcs that the ship was coming. You might have even warned them that you were coming when you sent out a bunch of messages about your “Don’t trust anybody because you have doppelgangers,” before you left for the Peninsula.

time.basis: Dawn is spoken here; the later departure date at u2856–u2862 dates this same morning; year from YAML.

markers.reading: Preparations take about five hours; the ship leaves Uzgukhar after lunch, around 1 p.m. on May 12.

markers.reading: The dust examination shifts narration into its earlier history in the Mirror of the Past.

evidence.quote: Delwath: I think, mirror on the dust of Seeker.
Seeker: And the dust of Seeker. Okay, let's do it.
DM: Okay.
DM: You hold up the dust to the mirror, and the 1st thing you see is Amil’s fist flying at your face, and a crunch.

DM: And then you shift quickly backward, drifting as a cloud high in the sky, waiting, lingering above the Plaguelands where you've been told to be. You wouldn't actually know that. You just see that you're a cloud floating high above the Plaguelands.

DM: And then shifting back further, the form now, not the Seeker clone, standing in front of Apollyon. So you're looking at Apollyon's back, the front of the Seeker clone. Apollyon seems to be sitting in meditation, almost, his skeletal head bare, pale, strange echo of a cloud crown floating over his head, a black crown made of some kind of matte, black iron, with 4 dark dark gems. The same crown that you've seen on Fausto's head. But here, reflected in some sort of pale echo form.
DM: And as you watch, there seem to be tendrils leaking out of the crown and touching the unformed creature, and you watch as it slowly turns into Seeker.

DM: And then the partially formed body lying in a coffin, complete, but blank and unformed, not even in humanoid shape, and Apollyon standing over it, holding a book, reading from this book, glancing as he turns to pages, probably chanting something not in any language Delwath can recognize. And this seems to go on for a very, very long time, like the mirror shows the scene over and over again like this is months of work.

DM: And then slowly back to the stone of Apollyon’s prison. You see in the mirror the walls of this chamber that that you saw in Delwath’s scrying, 5 coffins which you can’t see now, just looking at the blank wall of Drankorian marble.
DM: Apollyon slowly chipping away at the edge of the stone. Must have taken decades to make enough dust for 5 people, but not formed until much, much later.

markers.note: The months and decades shown belong to the dust’s history; they do not advance the adventure clock.

yamlCheck.dateAnchor: The DM explicitly dates the ship departure to May 12, the following afternoon to May 13, and the allied Kenzo teleport to May 14. The year 1749 comes from YAML.
yamlCheck.explanation: The opening morning and same-day departure are followed by an overnight flight and May 13 morning resurrection, then the overnight simulacrum casting reaches May 14. Rest and the allied Kenzo teleport remain on May 14. Riswynn’s conflicting departure date in t15 does not alter this independently supported session span. The prior attack, piracy reports and historical mirror scenes do not extend the played interval.
